verdict.why: kaikki-de-de reads der Boden as [ˈboːdn̩]; the model wrote /ˈboːdən/

draft.emotion: solid and dependable, like the earth beneath your feet
notes: Plural: die Böden (with umlaut). For the floor of a room, you can also say 'der Fußboden'. Do not confuse with 'die Etage' or 'der Stock' (floor/storey of a building).

senses.definition: The surface inside a room that you walk on.

examples.text: Die Kinder sitzen auf dem Boden und spielen.
examples.translation: The children are sitting on the floor playing.

senses.definition: The solid outdoor surface of the earth, or the soil in which plants grow.

examples.text: Nach dem Regen war der Boden ganz nass.
examples.translation: After the rain, the ground was completely wet.

senses.definition: The lowest part or underside of a container, glass, or body of water.

examples.text: Auf dem Boden der Tasse war noch etwas Zucker.
examples.translation: There was still some sugar at the bottom of the cup.

draftBefore.emotion: solid and dependable, like the earth beneath your feet
notes: Use 'Boden' for the interior surface of a room (floor) or the outdoor surface of the earth (ground/soil).
In a house, 'Boden' often specifically refers to the attic (Dachboden) when used in certain regions, but standardly it is the floor.
